name: Miloš Žefran
title: Professor; Associate Department Head; Robotics Laboratory
fitReason: Substantive learned perception feeds physical bimanual surgical control, with a broader program in multimodal collaborative robot policies.

physicalEvidence.summary: March 2025 primary paper, later IROS 2025, executes learned segmentation and instrument-keypoint detection on a first-generation da Vinci/dVRK with stereo endoscope and ROS2. YOLO11/MaskDINO/Detectron2 feed online boundary estimation, automatic grasp/stretch and instrument motion over ex-vivo porcine liver specimens. The paper defines dissection as energy delivery along tissue rather than proof of completed organ separation; autonomous repeated pulling and full separation remain future work. Geometric/PCA planning and control are explicit, not an end-to-end learned action policy. Current lab roster and lead author Ki-Hwan Oh’s 2026 dissertation project independently establish Žefran’s advising and current UIC group attribution. Separate CRCD data collection and new ViT pose-estimation evaluation are not counted as additional autonomous deployments.

shortVisit.status: degree-only · SMUL limited to Ljubljana students
shortVisit.summary: Lab Opportunities page welcomes enrolled UIC undergraduate/graduate students and prospective PhD applicants, without an external short-visitor category. A genuine mentor invitation appears in Ljubljana’s SMUL network, but the parent program explicitly serves University of Ljubljana students; it is not a general external-master opening.
